sentence: This project studies how interferon affects sphingolipid metabolism and how these lipids in turn regulate innate antiviral responses.
This project studies aggregation of an RNA binding protein in neurodegenerative disease and how to generate replacement neurons in the brain.
This project tries to find out how T cells help B cells make antibodies against HIV infection and makes protein immunogens for vaccine studies.
This project uses sequencing technologies on postmortem Alzheimer's disease brains to find driver genes, then tests them in human cell models with genetic screens.
This project tests whether nanoparticles called supermeres keep cytotoxic T cells out of colorectal cancer tumors, using antibodies and mouse models.
This project uses machine learning and genetic risk scores to build a tool that predicts postpartum hemorrhage.
This project studies the molecular differences between dementia with Lewy bodies and Alzheimer's disease using postmortem brain tissue samples.
This project builds deep learning methods to analyze histopathological information in digital pathology.
This project develops technologies to uncover cellular and circuit dysfunction in early Alzheimer's disease.
This project studies how the E4 variant of a gene affects different cell types in the brain and drives Alzheimer's disease.
This project develops targeted blocking antibodies to shield transplanted organs from the patient's immune response.
This project builds a nanoelectrochemical measurement platform for single cell and spheroid metabolomics and pharmacokinetics.
This project tries to find out how a fibrotic microenvironment impairs T cell function in metastatic lung cancer and how to restore anti-tumor immunity.
This project develops a vaccine against syphilis that targets outer membrane proteins of the syphilis spirochete.
This project refines blood epigenetic tests to diagnose osteoarthritis in advance and predict which patients will progress rapidly.
This project studies how venous sinusoids support hematopoietic stem cells in the marrow, using zebrafish.
This project compares asymmetric walking protocols to find the optimal one for restoring healthy gait after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction.
This project studies how the frog Xenopus tropicalis regenerates its spinal cord after injury and why this fails after metamorphosis.
This project creates genetic tags and workflows to study receptor organization with fluorescence and electron microscopy.
This project studies how immunosuppressive treatment with mycophenolate mofetil changes protective immunity after vaccination in kidney transplant recipients.
